column1: # Easyport translation rules — Forge 1.20.1 -> NeoForge 1.21.1
# Lines are  kind <TAB> from <TAB> to  (to omitted for REMOVED). Blank lines and # ignored.
# Deliberately small. Under shim-first, most loader-API references need no rewriting at all:
# forge-compat ships a real net.minecraftforge.* tree, so a mod's existing references resolve
# against it untouched. Rules are only needed where a shim is impossible — which in practice
# means net.minecraft.*, since that package is owned by the game and cannot be shadowed.
# SRG -> official member renaming is not expressed here. It is 64,225 entries and lives in
# mappings/srg2official.tsv, applied automatically before any rule below is matched. Rules
# are therefore written against *official* names.
# Rule kinds
#   CTOR_TO_STATIC   a constructor became a static factory. Rewrites NEW/DUP/INVOKESPECIAL
#                    into a single INVOKESTATIC. Real bytecode surgery, not a rename.
#   RENAME_METHOD    same shape, different owner or name. A plain call-site rewrite.
#   REMOVED          no replacement exists. Reported, never silently rewritten -- inventing a
#                    target here is exactly the failure mode measured in handport/ (5 false
#                    positives out of 26 symbols).
# --- Loader-scanned annotations: the hard exception to shim-first -------------------------
# These MUST be rewritten and cannot be shimmed. FML discovers mods by scanning class files
# for the exact annotation descriptor `Lnet/neoforged/fml/common/Mod;`. A shimmed
# net.minecraftforge.fml.common.Mod in forge-compat is a *different type* as far as that scan
# is concerned, so the mod is never found and never constructed -- it loads, registers
# nothing, and reports no error, which is the worst possible failure mode.
# Measured: additional_lights translated cleanly, loaded, and contributed 0 of 326 entries
# purely because its @Mod annotation still said net.minecraftforge.
# The rule of thumb: anything the *loader itself* looks up by name must be rewritten.
# Everything a mod merely calls can be shimmed.
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
# --- Event types: dispatched by identity, so also unshimmable ---------------------------
# The event bus resolves a listener's target from the declared parameter type and dispatches
# by exact class. A shimmed FMLCommonSetupEvent would be a distinct class from the one the bus
# actually posts, so the listener would register successfully and then simply never fire --
# again silent, again the worst kind of failure.
# Same rule as the annotations above: the loader dispatches these, so they must be rewritten.
# A mod only *calls* ForgeConfigSpec, so that one can stay shimmed.
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
TYPE_RENAME
# --- ResourceLocation: constructor privatised in 1.21 -------------------------------------
# The single largest vanilla dependency in the corpus: 237 + 188 mods.
CTOR_TO_STATIC
CTOR_TO_STATIC
# 135 / 111 / 105 / 97 mods. These are NOT renames: the whole idiom changed, and a call-site
# rewrite cannot express getOrCreateTag() returning a mutable tag backed by the stack.
# Recorded as REMOVED so the transformer reports them instead of guessing. The vanilla bridge
# (Phase 4) is what actually resolves these.
REMOVED
REMOVED
REMOVED
REMOVED
# --- Formerly listed as removed; both are now shimmed ------------------------------------
# FMLJavaModLoadingContext#get and ModLoadingContext#get were recorded here as having no
# replacement, on the reasoning that NeoForge injects the bus into the mod constructor. That
# was wrong: NeoForge kept ModLoadingContext.get() and exposes the bus through
# getActiveContainer().getEventBus(), so both are plain delegating shims in forge-compat.
# Left as a note rather than deleted, because a stale REMOVED entry is actively harmful --
# every translation report flagged a resolved symbol as unresolvable, which sends whoever
# reads the report chasing work that is already done.
# --- Vanilla constructors whose arguments were reordered ---------------------------------
# CTOR_SWAP2  owner <TAB> oldDesc <TAB> newDesc <TAB> [narrowTopTo]
# TorchBlock went from (Properties, ParticleOptions) to (SimpleParticleType, Properties) in
# 1.21 -- reordered and narrowed at once. The narrowing needs a CHECKCAST emitted before the
# swap, while the value is still reachable on top of the stack.
CTOR_SWAP2
CTOR_SWAP2
# RENAME_METHOD  owner <TAB> name <TAB> desc <TAB> newOwner <TAB> newName <TAB> newDesc
# The kind a rename table handles well -- and the kind corpus mining scored 13 out of 13 on in
# the hand-port. Kept explicit rather than auto-imported from candidate-rules-strong.tsv so
# every entry has been checked; the mining is a source of leads, not of truth.
RENAME_METHOD
# TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME  fromPrefix <TAB> toPrefix
# A prefix rename is normally the wrong tool -- a blanket net.minecraftforge -> net.neoforged
# rename would defeat the shim layer entirely. It is correct here precisely because these
# packages contain nothing but event classes, and events are dispatched by exact class
# identity, so every one of them must be rewritten. Enumerating several hundred individually
# would be noise, and any that got missed would fail silently by simply never firing.
# Exact TYPE_RENAME entries above still win: they are checked first.
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
# Supersedes the nine individual FML lifecycle TYPE_RENAME entries above: net/neoforged/fml/
# event/ covers both the lifecycle and config trees, so one rule replaces them and there are
# eight fewer places for the list to drift out of date. Also picks up ModConfigEvent, which
# the hand-written list had simply missed.
TYPE_PREFIX_RENAME
# --- Removed vanilla types: relocate, then rename -----------------------------------------
# 1.21 deleted these outright. Supplying the class in its original package is impossible --
# net.minecraft is owned by the game's module and a second jar exporting into it fails module
# resolution (proven in testkit/vanilla-package-probe). So forge-compat carries a stand-in
# under easyport.vanilla and references are rewritten to it.
# Restores loading, not behaviour: vanilla drives loot serialization through codecs now and
# will never call the shim's methods, so custom loot conditions and functions stay inert. The
# rest of the mod works. Generating a codec from the mod's serialize/deserialize pair is
# Phase 4 vanilla-bridge work.
TYPE_RENAME
# Same shape as TorchBlock: 1.21 moved the Properties argument last. No narrowing needed here,
# both arguments are already the right types.
CTOR_SWAP2
